messages.author: 88cc50a7df20ac58
messages.subject: EFA WLSMV maximum sample sizes
parts:
So I'm trying to run some fairly large models with lavaan

Twofactor<-efa(data, nfactors=2, estimator = "WLSMV", rotation = "Oblimin")
The model has 55 items and N= 1498. The indicators are categorical but they are in the data frame as numeric rather than as factors.

I can run the model without rotation fine, but when I run it with the rotation I get the error, that others in this group have had, number of observations too small to calculate gamma, and it doesn't create a model at all.

I've been told that I should be able to run this model in MPlus and the sample size should be big enough. Why would the model run in MPlus but not in R using lavaan with the same sample size? Is there anything I can do to get the model to run? Do I need to somehow specify that the data is ordinal rather than continuous?

I am having similar issues with a 1 factor model that has 192 items and a sample size of N= 2997, this also produces the gamma error, even without the rotation specified.
Onefactor<-efa(bigdata, nfactors=1, estimator = "WLSMV")

Any help would be appreciated.

Danielle

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: EFA WLSMV maximum sample sizes
parts:
On 6/19/23 20:48, Dani Broxy wrote:
> So I'm trying to run some fairly large models with lavaan
>
> Twofactor<-efa(data, nfactors=2, estimator = "WLSMV", rotation = "Oblimin")
> The model has 55 items and N= 1498. The indicators are categorical but
> they are in the data frame as numeric rather than as factors.

If you don't add the ordered = TRUE argument, the indicators will be
considered as numeric. If this is intended, I would suggestion using ML
instead.

> I can run the model without rotation fine, but when I run it with the
> rotation I get the error, that others in this group have had, number of
> observations too small to calculate gamma, and it doesn't create a model
> at all.

Hm. If you have 55 items, the dimension of Gamma is 55*56/2 = 1540
times 1540. Which is too large for N=1498. I am surprised this works
without rotation. (Are you using rotation = "none"?).

> I've been told that I should be able to run this model in MPlus and the
> sample size should be big enough.

> I am having similar issues with a 1 factor model that has 192 items and
> a sample size of N= 2997, this also produces the gamma error

If you treat the data as (semi-)continuous, change the estimator to ML.
If you treat the data as categorical (ordered = TRUE), change the
estimator to ULS.

Yves.

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: EFA WLSMV maximum sample sizes
parts:
Hi Danielle,

I believe that the default rotation method is geomin, but there are other possibilities as well (see below).

rotation: Character. The rotation method to be used. Possible options are varimax, quartimax, orthomax, oblimin, quartimin, geomin, promax, entropy, mccammon, infomax, tandem1, tandem2, oblimax, bentler, simplimax, target, pst (=partially specified target), cf, crawford-ferguson, cf-quartimax, cf-varimax, cf-equamax, cf-parsimax, cf-facparsim, biquartimin, bigeomin. The latter two are for bifactor rotation only. The rotation algorithms (except promax) are similar to those from the GPArotation package, but have been reimplemented for better control. The promax method is taken from the stats package.

Best wishes,

Jasper
